title: input validate regex runs with no timeout on the UI thread — a pathological pattern freezes the whole app
existing_state: InputCommand compiles the user-supplied `validate:` pattern with `new Regex(step.Input.Validate, RegexOptions.Compiled)` and no match timeout (Services/Scripting/Commands/InputCommand.cs:41). The match executes in the dialog's OK handler on the UI thread (`_validationRegex.IsMatch(_txtInput.Text)` in BtnOk_Click, InputCommand.cs:209). A backtracking-prone pattern (e.g. `^(\w+\s?)*$`) combined with a longish non-matching input hangs the entire WinForms message pump indefinitely — no Stop button, no recovery except killing the process. The codebase already has the fix pattern: ScriptRegexDefaults.UserPatternTimeout (5s, Services/Scripting/ScriptRegexDefaults.cs:10) is used for the same class of user-authored patterns in ExtractCommand.cs:60 and ExpressionEvaluator.cs:98 — input validation is the one place it was missed.
recommendation: Pass ScriptRegexDefaults.UserPatternTimeout as the third Regex constructor argument at InputCommand.cs:41, and catch RegexMatchTimeoutException in BtnOk_Click (treat as validation failure with a 'pattern timed out' message). Optionally drop RegexOptions.Compiled, which buys nothing for a few interactive matches.
user_benefit: A typo'd validation regex in a script can no longer hard-freeze the app mid-fleet-run at an interactive prompt, taking the unsent work of the whole run with it.

evidence.note: IsMatch on the UI thread in BtnOk_Click
5s UserPatternTimeout exists and is used by extract and the expression evaluator
